setlist.title: It's All Over Now, Baby Blue

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Little Red Rooster** (5 reviews): Reviewer calls it their favorite version, with tight interplay and extended jamming in the standard sections; Reviewer considers this the best Rooster ever [21][23][24][29][30]
- **Mexicali Blues** (1 review): Standard performance, hurt by weak Weir vocals [29]
- **Brown-Eyed Women** (1 review): More successful than Mexicali; Jerry's inflection added poignancy [29]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 review): Lovelight singled out as a standout of the show, followed by the Baby Blue encore [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **Technical Problems**: back after 308 archived shows (1704 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [31]
- **PA Music**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-04-10.sbd.unknown.mtownshend.102188.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 135 min; rated 1.33/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd1987-04-10.nak300.gidley.andrewf.93385.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 133 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]
- **gd1987-04-10.146111.mtx.tobin.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 137 min [6]
- **gd1987-04-10.167472.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 134 min [7]
- **gd87-04-10.nak.braverman.10537.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 129 min; rated 4.25/5 by 16 [13]. Said about its sound: Sound is a little hollow, rated three to four stars, but not an obstacle to enjoying the show; Recording sounds muddy and distant, with problems in the recording levels [24][25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer sat on the aisle steps after the show, staring at the stage, stunned by how the music sounded [19]
- Reviewer sat front row of the balcony on Brent's side, roughly 40 feet away [20]
- A couple of tunes into set II, Phil went to the mike and shouted 'You guessed it!' [20]
- With the crowd going wild, Phil redirected the applause to the drummers, Billy and Mick [21]
- Many teases in this show foreshadow the following day's fairly predictable setlist [28]
- Local women guarding the doors made hysterical comments, seemingly bewildered by the vortex of energy [30]
- Reviewer felt energy circulated between band and audience in a perfect circle [30]
- Reviewer credits this night and the one before for their deep love of the band; each hit differently [19]
- Reviewer says the night won them back to the Dead after mid-80s shows when the band seemed to have lost it [22]
- Reviewer ranks the show among the best of 1987 [23]
- Sound is acceptable compared with the crappy cassettes that circulated before today's better-quality sources [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-04-10.sbd.unknown.mtownshend.102188.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by mtownsend; source: SBD Unknown [1]
- **gd1987-04-10.nak300.gidley.andrewf.93385.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Ted Gidley; transferred by Andrew F.; source: OTS AUD: Nakamichi CM300's w/CP4 shotguns > Sony TC-D5M > Maxell MX-90's, with no Dolby. [2]. Also: Nakamichi 300 source; a patch from ShnID-10537 covers the tape flip in Space, 3:37 to 3:43 [2]
- **gd1987-04-10.146111.mtx.tobin.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Kevin Tobin; source: SBD + AUD Matrix 2 Source Mix (44/16) [6]. Also: A mix made by an archive.org user, converted to FLAC in April 2019 by Trader Little Helper [6]
- **gd1987-04-10.167472.senn.me80.hessberg.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Michael Hessberg; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Michael Hessberg's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser ME-80 mics > Sony D5M [7]. Also: A Nakamichi 304 source from Ted Gidley and Andrew F supplies the first 1:12 of Shakedown Street [7]
- **gd87-04-10.nak.braverman.10537.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Cassette (Nakamichi 300/Sony D5) [13]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-04-09 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-09-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [32]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1987-04-11 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-11-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [33]
- Poster by Ron Delany Grateful Dead: [1987-04-10 UIC Pavilion, Chicago, IL, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-04-10-uic-pavilion-chicago-il-usa/) [34]

Reviewer felt energy circulated between band and audience in a perfect circle
